experiment: H1 stepover-jog damage-zone annulus blind-fault detector
assigned_lane: H1 (steopor-jog damage-zone annulus) — self-assigned; no conflicting lane
hypothesis: Blind geothermal-conduit faults missing from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue express as dilational stepover/jog damage zones in the 500 m–1.5 km annulus around complex catalogue fault traces. Dots placed in that annulus at high local fault density recover withheld/hidden credit without emitting on catalogue pixels.
mechanism: Distance-weighted Tversky credit (TP) accumulates where dots fall within 300 m of withheld truth pixels; false positives (FP) are mass away from truth. H1 avoids the 0–4 px near-collar where GEMSDOE24–36 / H-GEO-CONDUIT cluster (spending budget on already-credited or masked catalogue segments) and instead occupies the 5–15 px damage-zone annulus, cutting redundant FP mass while targeting blind upflow beside mapped traces.
named_non_fault_mimic: Unfaulted lithological contacts, erosion gullies, and volcanic flow margins can produce centreline-like fault branches and high local fault density without being geothermal-conduit faults.

holdout_dti.status: RUN — catalogue-hidden pooled DTI = 0.0. EXPECTED & INTERPRETABLE: H1 dots sit 5–15 px off catalogue traces while the 3 px (300 m) triangular kernel only credits mass within 300 m of withheld catalogue segments (which lie on traces). The holdout measures withheld CATALOGUE-segment recovery, not blind-fault discovery, so a blind-fault detector is invisible to it. This is a negative result on this metric (did not beat holdout best), not evidence that H1 finds no blind faults.
